phrases.text: You can always tell.
The piece is fine, just unfinished.
The hedge is still in the sentence.
The point shows up in the last paragraph.
These are not careless people.
They know what a good piece looks like.
So why does the work arrive unfinished?
Look at where the day already goes.
3.4 hours of every working day, creating.
That time is doing real work.
It has to hold everything else you owe.
A second draft is not polish.
It is where the argument gets cut down.
It is where the vague sentence gets replaced.
It is where you find what you meant.
That is the work.
So it is the first thing dropped.
A first draft is publishable.
A second draft is optional.
Cutting it does not cost you speed.
It costs you the point.
So most published work is not the thinking.
It is the first attempt at thinking.
With a deadline attached.
So put the second draft on the calendar.
Not after the deadline, before it.
Publish the thought, not the attempt.
